cost_model_finding.question: Does A's band price include the 176,064 dense cells as native operations A really performs, which V really does not, and is the convention the one every earlier arm used?
cost_model_finding.what_A_does: klein_v4::build_echelon (src/cryptanalysis/klein_v4.rs:1203 at 9b2a47238b) allocates every Macaulay row as vec![0u16; cols.len()]: 393 rows x 448 columns = 176,064 u16 cells materialised and zero-written per call (system allocator, calloc of 896-byte heap chunks, memset on reuse), then about 1.12e4 coefficient writes. E33's counted echelon (gaudry_quartic::echelon_by_lead_counted, gaudry_quartic.rs:1624-1650) then scans each row from column 0 to its lead, reading the zero prefix (73,630-73,632 first-scan reads per call, Stage 0). Nothing later touches the prefix: row updates run on [c, cols) (gaudry_quartic.rs:1736-1746), the reachability pass and the left-looking normal forms read a pivot row right of its pivot (klein_v4.rs:1776-1793, 1813-1839). So A performs at least two native operations on each of the 73,237-73,239 prefix cells (one write, one read) and the band charges it one per cell of the whole matrix.
cost_model_finding.what_V_does: macaulay_profile::build_profile (macaulay_profile.rs:569) allocates vec![0u16; ncols - start] with start the column of LM(f_i)*shift (Stage 0: the row's lead on every one of 4,400 calls): 102,749-102,827 cells per clean call; echelon_profile's first scan reads one cell per row; every update, normalisation and normal-form substitution runs on the same column ranges through the offset, with the same multiplication counts. The identity (total_muls, every phase count and the pivot digest on 10,000/10,000 Stage A calls; 32/32 + 20/20 end-to-end rows equal outside the allowed fields) shows the arithmetic is A's. V therefore does not perform the 73.2e3 prefix writes or the 73.2e3 prefix reads per call.
cost_model_finding.same_convention: Every arm of this line since E24/E25 is priced S(g) = total_muls + 97 g x (one native operation per Macaulay cell built: rows*cols at the last degree, x2 on a chain-solve fallback) + counted selection work; E31 (note 9.22-9.24), E32, E33 and E35-E39 used it unchanged, and the E24, E25, E31, E32 validators accepted it ('Macaulay-matrix entry traffic, emitted as macaulay_entries'). V's macaulay_stored_entries is the same quantity for V's data structure (the cells V builds), and V's added work (each use of a row offset, 22,340-22,489 per call) is charged at the same rate. On a fallback call V is charged A's 2*rows*cols plus its failed attempt's offset operations, so V is never cheaper there (Stage A: 63/63 fallback calls charged A's cells; end to end: (A entries - V stored) per clean call is 73,237.2-73,238.0 on all 32 rows and inside the Stage 0 prefix range on all 20 A'/V' rows, i.e. fallbacks carry identical cells).
cost_model_finding.not_bytes: The cell count is an entry count, not a byte count: the 2026-11-01 owner rule (AGENTS.md 5a, NON_OPERATION_COUNTERS in ecbench/band.rs) exempts only memory-size counters, and the byte-counter audit (research/ic_byte_counter_pricing_20261101/README.md) treats entry counts (residual_table_entries) as operations. A cell is materialised by a write, so it is priced as one.
cost_model_finding.not_accounting: The algorithm changed (the data structure and the native work it performs), the counter definition did not: A's records keep macaulay_entries = rows*cols unchanged (V's records carry the same value; V is priced on the new field only).
cost_model_finding.not_relabelling: No work moved to an unpriced place: V's added offset arithmetic is priced; its lead-scan reads (unpriced in the main band, priced in sigma1) also fell 79,114-79,117 -> 5,877-5,879 per call; sigma1 and sigma4 keep every order.
limits_the_board_must_carry: At 0 GAE (counted F_p multiplications, the unit of every S column) V = A exactly on every call and every row: no arithmetic was saved.

The 1.25x / 1.37x at 0.1 / 1 GAE price one u16 cell (a vectorised zero-write) at 9.7 / 97 F_p multiplications. The band is a sensitivity range, not a calibration: at 0.01 GAE per cell the same records give 1.060-1.065x, at 0.001 GAE 1.0070-1.0077x (validator's Stage A recompute, not a claim of E40). No wall-time claim exists.

Work common to both arms that neither emits (the F_p additions paired with every counted multiplication, the dense-update cell traffic of the echelon) would, if priced, shrink S_A/S_V toward 1; it cannot reverse the order, because V does the same arithmetic and updates and strictly fewer cell operations, with its added work charged.

The rank is the registered weak one: equal at 0 GAE, strictly ahead at 0.1 and 1 GAE on 32/32 rows. Since S(g) is linear in g with equal intercepts and V's slope strictly smaller on every row, V is ahead at every positive weight, including a GAE of 79 or 66.5 F_p multiplications instead of the registered 97.
